judge_assessment.explanation: ACCEPT is right and the one recorded error is real. final_response.md describes the worksheet as '(ws_remainders_curr113.pdf, 3 pages)'; pdfinfo reports Pages: 5. The answer-key and study-guide counts in the same paragraph (2 and 2) are accurate, so only the worksheet number is wrong. On the substance the judge is also right that coverage is complete: I recomputed every value - floor(53/6) = 8, 47 - 5*9 = 2, ceil(128/9) = 15, floor(275/8) = 34, ceil(350/6) = 59, 623 - 9*69 = 2, 240/40 = 6 and 237 - 40*5 = 37, floor(1248/9) = 138, ceil(2455/8) = 307 and 2455 - 8*306 = 7, ceil(314/6) = 53 and 314 - 6*52 = 2 - and every one matches the key and the worksheet. Critically for this shard, the three multi-part problems (7, 9, 10) each carry a separate entry per part, so a right part (a) cannot cover a wrong part (b): this is the discipline the shard's rejected cases lack. I also checked the two canonical systemic defects against the artifacts and neither applies - no stem asks for an explanation (problem 10's find-and-fix asks only for two numbers), so the zero-manual claim is honest, and final_response.md names all three PDFs by filename. The one thing I would add to the judge's account is that the delivery also asserts '6-6.5 cm of work space per single-part problem'; that claim IS accurate, but it is sourced from worksheet.tex's \problem[6cm] arguments, not from verify.json, which declares no workspace_cm at all.

strengths_to_preserve: Multi-part coverage done right: problem 7 carries `estimate` 237/40 -> 6 AND `eval` 237 - 40*floor(237/40) -> 37; problem 9 carries ceiling -> 307 AND remainder -> 7; problem 10 carries ceiling -> 53 AND remainder -> 2. One entry per printed answer line. This is exactly the pattern the rest of the shard is missing and it should be held up as the reference.

The three remainder meanings are encoded as three distinct expression shapes - floor(a/b), ceiling(a/b) and a - b*floor(a/b) - so each interpretation is independently recomputed rather than derived from a single quotient. A sheet whose whole point is 'the same division, three answers' verifies it that way.

The study guide runs its first three sections off ONE division, 74 / 8 = 9 R 2, so the student sees the identical computation produce 9, 10 and 2 depending on the question. That is the cleanest possible teaching of this focus and it matches the requested rule / worked example / try-it shape.

Problem 10 plants a wrong INTERPRETATION rather than a wrong computation: Maya's 314 / 6 = 52 R 2 is arithmetically correct and her conclusion '52 boxes are needed' is not. The 52 is declared as a machine-checked trap distinguishable from 53, which is the right way to test this focus.

The boxed decision guide at the top names the only three things a remainder can mean, and the directions require writing the division, quotient and remainder before choosing - so the sheet teaches a decision procedure rather than a computation.

root_causes.description: The page counts in final_response.md are written by hand from intent rather than read back from the compiled PDFs, so the worksheet is described as 3 pages when the artifact the user receives is 5. The build already knows the real number - the page-budget gate compiles each document and compares its page count against a budget - but that value is never fed into the delivery text.
evidence: pdfinfo worksheet.pdf reports Pages: 5; the same file's answer key (2) and study guide (2) claims are correct.
scripts/page_budget.py already computes and compares per-document page counts during the gate chain.

improvements.title: Generate the delivery response's page counts from the compiled PDFs instead of writing them by hand
improvements.proposed_change: Have build.sh emit the three compiled page counts as a machine-readable line in gate_log.txt (for example 'PAGES ws=5 ak=2 ss=2') and instruct in SKILL.md's delivery section that the response's page counts must be copied from that line, never estimated. Optionally have build.sh write a small delivery_facts.json next to the PDFs holding the filenames and page counts, so the response is assembled from measured values.
improvements.regression_test: Add a test that builds a fixture whose worksheet compiles to 5 pages, writes a final response claiming 3, and asserts a new check fails. Simpler variant: assert gate_log.txt contains the PAGES line with the true counts - it does not today.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes a recurring credibility defect: three of the ten cases in this shard (curr-113, curr-126, curr-138) and curr-144's answer-key count all misstate a page count in the delivery.
improvements.risk: Very low. The change is additive to the gate log and the delivery text; nothing in the compiled documents changes.

case_summary: The strongest instruction-following case in the shard and a genuine ACCEPT. Ten remainder-interpretation problems in real contexts, every value independently confirmed, three distinct verification shapes for the three remainder meanings, and - unusually for this run - a separate check for every part of every multi-part problem, so the coverage gap that sank six of my other nine cases simply is not present here. Nothing on the sheet asks for an explanation, so the zero-manual claim is honest, and the delivery names all three PDFs by filename. The single defect is cosmetic but real: the delivery calls the worksheet 3 pages when it is 5, because page counts are narrated rather than read back from the compiled files.
